questions.question: As per the RBI’s final co-lending norms, what is the minimum percentage of each individual loan that entities in a Co-Lending Agreement (CLA) must retain?
questions.explanation:
• The correct answer is option 'C' that is '10%'.
  • The RBI’s final co-lending norms mandate that entities involved in a CLA must retain at least 10% of each individual loan on their own books.
  • This ensures that both lending partners share the credit risk and remain committed to maintaining loan quality.
  • The originating entity in a co-lending arrangement is allowed to provide a Default Loss Guarantee (DLG) up to 5% of the outstanding loan amount sanctioned under the CLA. This acts as a partial credit risk cover for the partner entity.
  • The RBI has allowed a transition period for existing CLAs to adjust to the new framework. All such agreements must comply with the updated co-lending norms by January 1, 2026.

questions.question: As of September 2025, under Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), India’s fish production reached 195 lakh tonnes in 2024–25, marking a 104% increase since 2013–14. When was the PMMSY launched?

questions.question: From which season has the Government of India allowed unrestricted ethanol production from sugarcane juice, syrup, and all types of molasses?

questions.question:
Match the RBI regulation-making feature with its description:

  1. Public Consultation Period

  2. Final Regulation Draft

  3. Review of Existing Rules

  4. Exemptions

a) RBI’s written response to stakeholder comments
b) 21 days minimum for citizens’ feedback
c) Removing outdated provisions and duplication
d) Internal administration, minor procedures, urgent actions
questions.explanation:
Answer: A) 1-b, 2-a, 3-c, 4-d

  • Public consultation = minimum 21 days

  • Final draft = includes RBI’s response to comments

  • Review = remove outdated rules, global alignment

  • Exemptions = internal/urgent/procedural cases

In May 2025, the RBI rolled out a new framework for making regulations to bring transparency, accountability, and global alignment to its rule-making process.

  • Key Features: Draft regulations will be published online with objectives, legal basis, and impact analysis. Stakeholders (citizens, banks, industry) get 21+ days to provide feedback. The final regulation must include RBI’s written responses.

  • Flexibility: If post-feedback changes are major, the consultation process may be repeated. RBI can also use discussion papers for broader engagement.

  • Review of Old Rules: Regular revisions will remove outdated provisions and duplication, aligning India’s regulatory ecosystem with international best practices.

  • Exemptions: The framework excludes internal administrative matters, minor tweaks, and urgent/confidential actions (like crisis-driven moves).

questions.question:

II. Some majority of houses, shops and carts dama­ged in the Jahanpur demolition drive.
III. The trio has been reportedly accused of setting a motorbike on fire.
questions.explanation:
Sentence I: This sentence contains a subject-verb agreement error. The subject "procession" is singular, so the verb should also be singular. Instead of "have resulted", the correct phrase should be "had resulted" if indicating past perfect, or "has resulted" if referring to the present perfect tense. Given the context that the event already happened and resulted in injuries, "had resulted" would be the most appropriate.

Sentence II: The phrase "some majority" is incorrect. "Majority" is a quantifier that doesn’t need "some" before it. The correct construction is "a majority of houses, shops, and carts were damaged...". Also, there’s an issue of missing auxiliary verb (“were”), which is implied in passive construction. So this sentence has both structural and article usage errors.

Sentence III: This sentence is grammatically correct. The word "trio" is a collective noun and is treated as singular in formal English, making "has been" appropriate. The structure and usage here are correct.

Correct answer: Option C (Both I and II).

The revised sentence would read: "The sheer fact that this is happening is a testament to how quickly the region is changing."
